A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Conformal Structured Prediction by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.2 report original coverage and prediction-set-size experiments on MNIST, ImageNet, and SQuAD, including five-run summaries and a qualitative example.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A.2–A.4 report original experiments on five domains, including baseline comparisons, runtime measurements, and qualitative prediction examples.

M1.justification: The cumulative-score optimization, descending threshold search, marginal/PAC tests, and DAG integer program are retained. The new code and emotion experiments instantiate this framework through domain-specific DAGs and scores; no redesign of the core calibration or optimization procedure is documented.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from three domains to five: v2 adds MBPP Python code completion with partial-program prediction sets and GoEmotions emotion prediction on English Reddit comments. The MNIST, ImageNet, and SQuAD year-answering tasks remain.

E2.justification: V2 introduces a baseline adapted from Khakhar et al. (2023), generalized to DAGs with monotonicity restrictions, and evaluates its coverage, prediction-set sizes, and runtime. V1 cited that work but lacked these systematic comparisons, providing model-accuracy/reference lines and illustrative standard-conformal examples instead.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported default m from 2 to 4 and replaces epsilon=0.4 with 0.15 in the sweep. New protocols include GPT-4o-mini completion from supplied ground-truth code prefixes and RoBERTa-base emotion prediction. Appendix A.2 introduces per-IP, threshold-estimation, and full-task timing measurements; the coverage and set-size metrics remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's hyperparameter sweeps and SQuAD example, v2 adds computational-cost and scalability analyses across DAG structures and m values (Appendix A.2). Appendix A.3 adds an ImageNet hyperparameter case study, a standard-PAC comparison, and two code examples showing which AST components become uncertain.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report averages and standard deviations over five runs. V2 extends that reporting to additional results without documenting increased repetition, new confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Shaded uncertainty bands replace some error-bar displays without changing the stated statistical practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds baseline results, MBPP and GoEmotions coverage/size curves, and runtime measurements. Figure 3 reports generally smaller SQuAD sets than the added baseline; Figure 8 shows runtime advantages in most tested domains but a disadvantage on 3-digit MNIST. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated performance gains over v1 under identical settings. Table 1's example intervals remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the MNIST decoding definition from a digit weight of 10^(k+1-i) to 10^(k-i), matching the existing 120–129 example. Theorems 3.1–3.2, their supporting arguments, and optimization equations (1)–(8) are otherwise retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a general structured-conformal framework, marginal/PAC coverage guarantees, and DAG-based prediction-set optimization. The additional domains and comparisons expand supporting evidence without redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of computational limitations, DAG density, unusually expensive m settings, and the inability to warm-start across varying code ASTs. It also clarifies that the DAG structures prediction sets rather than necessarily the label space, explains marginal versus PAC deployment choices, and expands guidance on the interpretability/granularity tradeoff.

D1.justification: V2 adds model and AST-scoring details for the new tasks, ImageNet's n=200 disclosure, DAG dimensions, and warm-starting information, and updates the advertised code address. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit SQuAD calibration/test split of 131/131 while retaining the 262-example total. This omission does not establish an actual split change.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands distinctions from Mortier, Quach, and Mohri–Hashimoto, including objectives, interpretability, and restricted search spaces. V2 newly discusses Angelopoulos et al. (2021) and (2024) on regularized prediction sets and risk control, and positions the evaluated Khakhar adaptation against its nonmonotone search. New dataset/model references accompany the added domains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most core exposition remain intact. V2 makes localized prose corrections and explanatory expansions, introduces dedicated runtime and qualitative appendix subsections, removes the standalone ethics/reproducibility statements, and adds acknowledgements and the conference header. Much of the added length represents new evidence rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: V1's separate example and framework diagrams become panels of v2 Figure 1. Quantitative plots are redrawn with revised axis ranges, dashed baseline curves, and uncertainty shading. V2 also adds runtime bar charts, an ImageNet comparison and table, and code AST diagrams, substantially expanding and reorganizing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The baseline comparisons and computational-cost analysis address important gaps in v1's evidence for comparative usefulness and practicality. Code-completion experiments also test a substantially different output structure, strengthening support for generality. Although omission of the explicit SQuAD split weakens reproducibility slightly, the added comparative evidence, informative examples, and candid runtime limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
